sentences: A fixed two-qubit interaction can be repeatedly applied to build a larger quantum computation.
This conjecture asks whether every such interaction falls into one of two computational regimes in the source's model.
One regime permits efficient classical simulation, while the other becomes universal when postselection is allowed.
The cited classification proves this dichotomy for commuting Hamiltonians, but ancillary qubits and encoded subspaces complicate the general case.
A complete classification would organize elementary interactions by computational power and rule out intermediate behavior between the proposed alternatives.
